Radtel RT-950 Pro Backup & Restore Firmware

nicsure

10. Juni

This firmware is designed specifically for the Radtel RT-950 Pro. I do not own a standard RT-950 (non-Pro), so I have no idea whether it will work on those models.

This is an important step that every RT-950 Pro owner should complete. Being able to write a storage back-up to the radio will be vital when restoring the original firmware.

Unlike the RT-880, I'm unable to "share" flash memory on the RT-950 Pro between stock and nicFW, so having a personal backup of your radio's flash is essential.

Flashing the Backup & Restore Firmware

Written instructions here
https://github.com/nicsure/RT-950-Pro-Web-Flasher

Or just watch the video above.

Included Factory Backup

I've also attached a flash backup taken from a brand-new, out-of-the-box RT-950 Pro:
flashbackup_new_radio.950spi

This is provided as a safety net for anyone who forgets to create their own backup before experimenting in the future. That said, I strongly recommend taking a backup of your own radio before making any changes.

Anhänge

rt950pro_flash_backup_restore.btf

flashbackup_new_radio.950spi

Also double check the ADC before performing any battery related action. Enforce the TX Cooldown globally so TX cannot be re-engaged until at least two seconds after the last TX ended to rule out any potential PTT bouncing problems. This time will eventually be shortened. Set the battery ADC reading function to keep a history of the last 4 readings, from which it picks the highest. This means it takes 4 consecutive low readings to trigger any low battery related action. If you wondered where the old post went. That 30 minute driver wasn't too stable and crashed CHIRP a lot, so I deleted that one. So here's v4. It should deal with channels, groups and settings. Use the comment field of the channels to set the group letters, so to put a channel in groups E and P for example, put 'PE' into the comment field for the channel. Group names can be changed in settings. Remember this is very quick delve into this using Codex, I'm not going to turn CHIRP into the RMS in half an hour, just bear that in mind. To install: Download the .py file from this post Put CHIRP into developer mode. 'Help -> Developer Mode' Restart CHIRP Select 'File -> Load Module' Browse to the downloaded .py file and select it Select 'Radio -> Download from radio' and choose the nicFW option at the bottom of the 'Vendor' list Click 'OK'

The upcoming release of nicFW880 v5.14.01 required a reshuffling of the flash memory map. While this was common during alpha and beta stages, I really tried to avoid it on full releases. However, on this release it simply couldn't be helped, this means: A factory reset will be required before flashing 5.14.01 Take a backup of your codeplug, power and calibration settings BEFORE flashing 5.14.01 with the previous RMS, then restore it after flashing with the new RMS. RMS versions must match, there's no leeway this time. My apologies for the inconvenience, there hopefully shouldn't be any more releases that will require this. V5.14.01 will be available soon, please make sure you have all taken codeplug, power and calibration backups in preparation. I think we're getting very close to a stable and feature complete firmware. At least I really hope so, it'll allow me to focus more on the RT-950.

2. Februar

17

5

I made a massive mistake. I tried to take the whole 880 code base, I literally copied the entire project file for file to a new 950 project. Then started on converting things over, the hardware, the interrupts, the DMA, everything all at once in a complete zoo of code, all while trying to keep track of what files I'd changed, what I hadn't etc. The MCU was significantly different despite being the same manufacturer and family which I also hadn't really bargained on, I figured they'd be similar enough that this approach would be okay. Bad idea! One problem led to another and to another until I was just so mixed up and jumbled in the code and my own head that my head gasket blew. I know now I should have approached this as I have all other conversions and re-writes I've done. Do it file by file, feature by feature, methodically, solving each problem sequentially and in an ordered fashion so I'm not stressing about a huge tree of branching issues stretching into infinity. I'm pretty much back to full motivational heights, but this seven days away at my friend's is going to act as a final binary detox, no computers, no code, no stress. Just sampling some real ale and enjoying some nice single malts. Then I'll get cracking on doing this the right way. I've been blown away by the positive energy of this community and the overwhelming support you've all shown me, so thank you all for that, deeply, it's really helped. Marcus

Please make sure you read and understand the previous release notes before posting any comment. I do not repeat myself in these release posts. What's New in 05F? Remote Button Labels (T9 and others) Added T9 (and related) labels to the remote buttons in the RMS for improved usability. Mixed VFO Support in Multiwatch Previously, mixing HF and non-HF VFOs in Multiwatch was disallowed because it caused rapid switching of the HF band-switch relay (annoying noise and extra relay wear). Now the HF band-switch relay is suppressed during Multiwatch checks so the active VFO is dominant for relay state. Mixed VFOs can be used; any VFOs that would require toggling the relay are skipped during checks. APRS Updates : RAW GPS (NMEA) Beacon decoding implemented. Standard APRS Beacon decoding implemented. Compressed APRS Beacon decoding implemented. Fixed: Unsquelched reception during APRS pop-ups when Hear Tones is enabled. Spectrum Scope improvements: Now has its own function menu . LP-Green Monitor signal trigger added (note: a regular scan is still the better tool for doing this, but the trigger is here for completeness). To activate use LP 0-9 to set a trigger level (LP-0 = Disable) . A blue line will appear on the scope to show the trigger level. Added FM, AM, DSB functions to the scope key functions. LP S1 = FM LP S2 = AM LP EMG = DSB Also selectable via the function menu. The Main Menu can now be accessed during Scope operation. Tuner mode scanning : Scanning will not start until the user releases the LP key (LP1 or LP3). Scanning is paused while a key is pressed, which also helps avoid overruns when stopping scans. Scanning speed improved. BETA 05G Update Ignore/exclude frequency in spectrum scope monitor mode (same as when scanning; press # while monitoring to exclude) Fixed issue with scope settings resetting after closing menus. Exit scope during monitoring and remain on the monitored frequency by pressing PTT. Added " Clear Ignores " key function to scope. Fixed issue of modulation changes in the scope "sticking" after exiting the scope. GPS distance calculation now corrects for latitude. (Longitude lines "squash" together as you get closer to the poles) Preventing the scope starting when in channel based modes. Removed " Beacon TX " to prevent confusion, as people don't seem to understand its purpose. Continue to use RMS 05F with this update. [-OSX RMS DOWNLOAD HERE-]

⚠️ BEFORE FLASHING CUSTOM FIRMWARE, MAKE SURE YOU HAVE A STORAGE BACKUP. Storage Backup Instructions ⚠️ RMS V6.00.09b IS REQUIRED This firmware will only work with RMS V6.00.09b . Older versions of RMS will not work with this release. Downloads for Windows, Linux and macOS are provided below. ⚠️ YOUR EXISTING SETTINGS WILL NOT BE RETAINED This release will not retain settings from the previous firmware version . I recommend performing a storage reset anyway: Hold the bottom side button while switching the radio on. BETA STATUS Most of the bugs found during the initial porting work have now been addressed, so I'm moving the firmware into the Beta stage . There are still areas being actively developed and tested, but the core port is now at the point where wider testing makes sense. AM TRANSMIT EXPERIMENT The AM transmit experiment is included in this release. It's still very much experimental. At the moment it doesn't perform particularly well at higher power settings, and the audio can sound a little scratchy. I'll continue working on improving it. The documentation has been updated with the relevant settings and explanations: https://github.com/nicsure/RMS880/wiki/Advanced-Menu#am-emulation-notes ⚠️ IMPORTANT AM transmit has not been soak tested , so there is a possibility of hardware damage. Please only experiment with this feature if you are comfortable accepting that risk. I'll continue testing it myself to see whether my radio eventually pops its clogs , so if you're not comfortable with the risk, you may wish to wait until I have more data. The later versions from 10b onward use a different method of AM generation that is far less likely to cause hardware issues. You cannot accidentally transmit in AM . A warning screen is displayed before AM transmit can be enabled. The RT-880 cannot use this method because of differences in its audio routing, so unfortunately this feature cannot be backported to the 880 . FOCUS MODE UPDATE When using Focus Mode, you can now stretch the VFO fonts to double height . Set: Advanced → Font Double → On Also, when you're in a channel or group setup, it can sometimes be difficult to tell which VFO is currently selected. The main icon bar now displays a I, II or III indicator showing which VFO is selected. CROSS-BAND REPEATER Cross-Band Repeater is now implemented. It works in the same way as the 880 version, with the addition of a monitoring function . The monitoring function is not possible on the 880 because of its different audio routing, so this part cannot be backported. v6.00.10b Update Continue to use RMS v6.00.09b with this until I can release an update to the RMS later. AM Transmit Improved significantly. Note: The ' AM TX Period' setting now does nothing. Only 'AM TX Depth' is relevant now. Smart Scan List is now persistent. User function 'Clr SmrtScan' added to clear the Smart Scan List. Fixed issue with LEFT button in channel mode. VFO Scans will now display a channel name if the scan frequency matches a stored channel. Added user function 'Ignore GW-CH' to exclude a nuisance channel from GroupWatch Default Key: SP-# Note: Previous settings will prevent the default key being applied, best to perform a Storage Reset anyway. v6.00.11b Update Keep using RMS v6.00.09b for now, I'll get the new RMS out soon. A Storage Reset is recommended. Tightened AM TX Audio on lower power settings. Changed AM receive method for HF frequencies. Re-introduced ' AM AGC Fix' in the 'Advanced' menu. Although I don't think it's needed anymore I added it back just in case. Added 'Ignore GroupWatch Channel' user function. Added 'RF-Gain' user function for the ARDF guys. When toggled on, AGC is disabled and a stepped bar icon appears to show RF-Gain is on manual. The noise bar will change to show the level of RF-Gain. Use the rotary encoder to alter the gain level. Note: With no AGC, strong signals can cause RX overload. Added 'Bandwidth' user function. VFO Scan will now display a channel name if the frequency matches a stored channel. 6.00.11x Update A few adjustments to the AM transmission system. Added a couple more fine tuning options in the advanced menu. AM Mic Gain Sets the level of microphone amplification for AM only. AM Envelope There are four preset envelopes (0 to 3). Select which one sounds best for you. AM Depth Sets the clipping window of the ADC audio capture. Lower values will produce more modulation but may introduce distortion if the microphone audio is too loud. The first thing I want to do is get RX audio to stream to the RMS while the remote is active. This is doable, using PortAudio it should work on all platforms too. The scan and record system naturally follows from that. The next goal will be TX audio. This is doable but tricker. Finally, once RX and TX audio can be streamed, this opens up networking. A server system can be connected to the radio and proxy the serial data over a network connection. Then a small remote app on an Android device could connect and fully operate the radio, from anywhere. I have already done this with Quansheng radios, but it was clunky and required an audio interface and a lot of setup. This would be much simpler. Another byproduct of this (if someone could write an Asterisk driver for it) is that a node could use a 950 and require only a USB cable. Anyway, that's the direction this avenue of features will be moving.

!!WARNING!! DO NOT use the RMS to flash this firmware. Use the Radtel Firmware Flashing Tool or the Web Based Flasher . ⚠️ BEFORE FLASHING CUSTOM FIRMWARE, MAKE SURE YOU HAVE A STORAGE BACKUP ⚠️ Storage Backup Instructions Community Support I 'maintain' a Telegram group and Facebook Group specifically for nicFW support and discussion. If you need some help or have a suggestion, by all means pop in and ask. If you're an advanced user, maybe consider hanging around and helping others. Click Here to go to the 'nicFW Hangout' on Telegram Click here to visit the nicFW Support page on Facebook Documentation nicFW is in Beta stage, meaning I'm focusing on features and bugs tracking, not creating documentation. However, since nicFW950 is mostly identical to nicFW880, the existing documentation Wiki will apply to 95% of operation. Where differences exist, the Wiki will be updated in time. Remember I'm just one guy. Click Here For The Wiki It is advised to perform a storage reset after flashing this firmware as critical default settings values have changed. Instructions for performing a Storage Reset RMS Downloads are attached below. I forgot to include the external microphone icon in the RMS' default fonts. You will need the attached ' symbols.rmsfont ' file and load it into the RMS before flashing other fonts to prevent losing the external microphone icon. What is the 'x' version? If you see a download attached to this release post with an 'x' suffix , this is what I call a preview release. A bit of a misnomer to be honest, but a word is just a word. When users report bugs or glitches, I work to fix them as quickly as possible. However, these fixes are often made alongside ongoing development, so the resulting firmware may also contain changes, improvements, or experimental features intended for the next full release. Think of it as going beyond the bleeding edge and well into the bandages! A little caution is advised when using these versions. They may contain unfinished or untested features, and some settings or functionality may not yet be supported by the RMS . Updates External microphone/headset support . ( Thanks Paul ) This means the mics and headsets specifically made for the 950. Do not use any other kind. I had to pretty much re-write the audio system to do this, so there may be audio glitches lurking under the bridge. AM/DSB TX has moved to an interrupt driven system. WARNING AM and DSB TX causes thermal stress to the radio's internal components. This is within the limits of what it was designed to tolerate on standard frequencies such as 11m, 2m and 70cm. But outside of those bands, the heating is in addition to the thermal stress transmitting on those bands causes naturally. This can be enough collectively to cause a shutdown due to overheating. AM TX also generates some wide band splatter, this is unfortunately unavoidable due to how the power output needs to be manipulated to achieve AM. So while AM transmission works, it isn't perfect. Advanced -> AM DSB TX Dp (Depth) Defines a normalization clipping window around the TX audio. Smaller windows will give wider audio response, larger windows will give clearer audio. It's a balance. Advanced -> AM DSB MGain (Mic Gain) Controls the amplifier gain that processes the microphone audio during AM/DSB TX. Advanced -> AM Envelope Sets the Post-Amble of the AM envelope. Larger values result in decreased output power but stronger audio, lower values give higher output power but weaker audio. AM TX SmplFrq (Sample Frequency) Sets the sample rate of the TX audio in kHz for AM and DSB. Higher frequencies give better audio clarity but eat more battery power. The new interrupt system can cause phase/beating audio artefacts, fine tuning of this setting can eliminate it. DSB Phase Fr (Frequency) Sets the frequency shift in dHz used to adjust the RF phase during DSB TX . This is a bit of a hack however, you will need to experiment. The modulation level bar will now work in AM mode. In DSB mode the actual power meter will deflect with audio modulation level. Note that DSB TX is not very good. This is an area I am continuing to experiment with however, but for now it sounds crap. The AM TX warning has been put back. But you only need accept it once. I needed to adjust the timings on channel scanning . As a result, the Channel Scan Speed you have set may feel slightly slower, just knock it up by 2 or 3 if so. Channel scanning speeds of 40 or more use a different scanning technique which is slightly faster. This will also apply to Multiwatch and Groupwatch too if set. The signal floor is now dynamically calculated from actual band conditions. Increased the range and defaults of the FM Deviation settings, as regular FM TX audio on this radio is very quiet at the same levels used for the RT-880. The modulation level bar now operates better visually. Small improvement on battery life. v6.00.15c Fixed audio ticking glitch in Tuner Mode while Multiwatch is enabled. Dropped the UHF threshold frequency to 200 MHz to allow better performance on 2 20 MHz AM/DSB Warning only appeared on DSB TX before, it now appears for both. Again it need only be accepted once. Fixed some settings not saving properly on power off due to not performing a settings sync after the setting is changed. I fixed by ensuring a sync occurs just before power-down. v6.00.15d I hit the 256k flash limit for firmware size, so I had to enable mild optimization. This affected timing and could have knock on effects. I think I've identified all of it though. Increased the Mic Gain setting so its high value is now 63 and changed the default to 48 . All deviation settings have been returned to their previous defaults. High TX Deviation causes hum on some radios, so I used another method of boosting TX audio. If you previously had a high TX Deviation , kick it back down to sensible values. Same goes for the Subtone Deviation and APRS Deviation . Note: The RMS still caps this to 31 of course. You'll have to live with this until 16b which will have the updated RMS . Returned the UHF split point to 280 MHz ( sorry about the 200 MHz debacle on 15c, I was misinformed, other testers confirmed that stock firmware and nicFW [pre 15c] performed the same on 220 MHz ). However, this split point may now be set in the Advanced menu. Maurizio Brameri identified a problem with the Storage Reset system, this version does not correctly wipe the radio. It will be fixed for the next build. v6.00.15e Fixed issue with Storage Reset not working correctly. Menu Shortcuts when linked to a number based menu now open the Main Menu with that item selected. BETA STATUS Most of the bugs found during the initial porting work have now been addressed, so I'm moving the firmware into the Beta stage . There are still areas being actively developed and tested, but the core port is now at the point where wider testing makes sense. AM TRANSMIT EXPERIMENT The AM transmit experiment is included in this release. It's still very much experimental. At the moment it doesn't perform particularly well at higher power settings, and the audio can sound a little scratchy. I'll continue working on improving it. The documentation has been updated with the relevant settings and explanations: https://github.com/nicsure/RMS880/wiki/Advanced-Menu#am-emulation-notes ⚠️ IMPORTANT AM transmit has not been soak tested , so there is a possibility of hardware damage. Please only experiment with this feature if you are comfortable accepting that risk. I'll continue testing it myself to see whether my radio eventually pops its clogs , so if you're not comfortable with the risk, you may wish to wait until I have more data. The later versions from 10b onward use a different method of AM generation that is far less likely to cause hardware issues. You cannot accidentally transmit in AM . A warning screen is displayed before AM transmit can be enabled. The RT-880 cannot use this method because of differences in its audio routing, so unfortunately this feature cannot be backported to the 880 . FOCUS MODE UPDATE When using Focus Mode, you can now stretch the VFO fonts to double height . Set: Advanced → Font Double → On Also, when you're in a channel or group setup, it can sometimes be difficult to tell which VFO is currently selected. The main icon bar now displays a I, II or III indicator showing which VFO is selected. CROSS-BAND REPEATER Cross-Band Repeater is now implemented. It works in the same way as the 880 version, with the addition of a monitoring function . The monitoring function is not possible on the 880 because of its different audio routing, so this part cannot be backported. v6.00.10b Update Continue to use RMS v6.00.09b with this until I can release an update to the RMS later. AM Transmit Improved significantly. Note: The ' AM TX Period' setting now does nothing. Only 'AM TX Depth' is relevant now. Smart Scan List is now persistent. User function 'Clr SmrtScan' added to clear the Smart Scan List. Fixed issue with LEFT button in channel mode. VFO Scans will now display a channel name if the scan frequency matches a stored channel. Added user function 'Ignore GW-CH' to exclude a nuisance channel from GroupWatch Default Key: SP-# Note: Previous settings will prevent the default key being applied, best to perform a Storage Reset anyway. v6.00.11b Update Keep using RMS v6.00.09b for now, I'll get the new RMS out soon. A Storage Reset is recommended. Tightened AM TX Audio on lower power settings. Changed AM receive method for HF frequencies. Re-introduced ' AM AGC Fix' in the 'Advanced' menu. Although I don't think it's needed anymore I added it back just in case. Added 'Ignore GroupWatch Channel' user function. Added 'RF-Gain' user function for the ARDF guys. When toggled on, AGC is disabled and a stepped bar icon appears to show RF-Gain is on manual. The noise bar will change to show the level of RF-Gain. Use the rotary encoder to alter the gain level. Note: With no AGC, strong signals can cause RX overload. Added 'Bandwidth' user function. VFO Scan will now display a channel name if the frequency matches a stored channel. 6.00.11x Update A few adjustments to the AM transmission system. Added a couple more fine tuning options in the advanced menu. AM Mic Gain Sets the level of microphone amplification for AM only. AM Envelope There are four preset envelopes (0 to 3). Select which one sounds best for you. AM Depth Sets the clipping window of the ADC audio capture. Lower values will produce more modulation but may introduce distortion if the microphone audio is too loud. APRS Problems still to resolve APRS needs to be handled a little differently on the RT-950-Pro because its audio system works differently from the RT-880. To decode APRS, the MCU needs to sample the received audio through an ADC. On both radios, this ADC is connected to the line-level audio output. There are also two controls that affect the audio: AMP_ENABLE – turns the audio amplifier on or off. AUDIO_MUTE – mutes the audio output. This is also used by the normal squelch system, and can sometimes be referred to as the SQUELCH_GATE . The important difference is how AUDIO_MUTE behaves on the two radios. On the RT-880 , muting the audio does not stop the ADC from receiving the audio signal. This means APRS can work alongside the normal squelch system without any special handling. When an APRS packet is received, the squelch can remain closed, muting the speaker, while the ADC can still receive the audio needed to decode the packet. The RT-950-Pro works differently. When AUDIO_MUTE is enabled, it completely removes the audio signal from the ADC as well. So if the squelch is closed, the APRS decoder has nothing to sample. For the RT-950-Pro, we therefore have to do the opposite: open the audio path so the ADC can receive the APRS signal . The problem is that this would also send the loud, unpleasant APRS tones to the speaker. The solution is to keep the audio path open for the ADC, but switch AMP_ENABLE off so the speaker remains silent. So, unlike the RT-880, APRS on the RT-950-Pro needs its own audio-handling logic: the squelch gate must be opened to allow the ADC to receive the packet, while the amplifier must be disabled to prevent the APRS tones from being heard. It's a relatively small hardware difference, but it means APRS can't simply use the normal squelch behaviour on the RT-950-Pro. macOS bundle https://github.com/nicsure/nicfw950-rms-builder/releases/tag/v6.00.07d

!!WARNING!! Perform a storage back BEFORE flashing these debug builds. nicFW overwrites the stock firmware's storage configuration which may make the stock firmware malfunction when flashing back. As the title implies, this version is meant for debugging. What I'm looking for are functional errors, not blanket statements like "The Tuner doesn't work" I know about things like that already. There will likely be a LOT of issues so please don't write a bunch of errors all in one post. I find that extremely difficult to manage. I like one error per post , that way I can concentrate on things one at a time without having to sift through a wall of text, then when I've fixed each one I can delete the post and thus work my way through things systematically. If that means making multiple posts then that's fine. Also remember to state which version of the debug firmware you're using. Of course I am fixing things all the time myself as I find them, so you may report something I've already fixed, but that's fine too. Just make sure you mention in the post what version you are testing with. This is the fun stage, but also the most demanding, but remember, these are NOT functional firmwares. They are meant to allow the community to help me debug the early builds. Please only flash them for that purpose.
